FIELD GUIDE · 2026

VOICE AGENT ENGINEERING · A BEGINNER GUIDE

Build the loop.
Measure the wait.

A voice agent is a timed event system. It listens, detects a completed turn, decides what to do, and starts the next spoken turn.

The agent task can change. The base system and the measurement method stay almost the same.

Start with the smallest version ↓
  1. 01ListenMicrophone audio
  2. 02Detect turnSpeech starts and stops
  3. 03UnderstandWords and intent
  4. 04DecideReply or tool call
  5. 05ActOptional external work
  6. 06SpeakAudio output

01 / SYSTEM

The base architecture

Keep the client, voice session, agent logic, and external tools separate. Add timestamps where data crosses each boundary.

CLIENT

Microphone + speaker

Captures audio. Plays audio. Shows connection and mute state.

⇄

VOICE SESSION

Transport + turn manager

Streams audio. Detects turns. Stops speech when the user interrupts.

⇄

AGENT RUNTIME

Instructions + state

Chooses a reply. Calls a tool when the task needs external work.

⇄

TOOLS

APIs + data

Reads or changes the application state. Returns a result to the agent.

OBSERVABILITY Audio, transcript, events, tool calls, errors, cost, and final state

TWO IMPLEMENTATION PATTERNS

Audio in→Speech to text→Text model→Text to speech→Audio out
BEST FOR

Learning each stage and inspecting transcripts.

TRADE-OFF

More stages add delay and more failure points.

BEGINNER VIEW

Start here if you want to see each component.

02 / TIMELINE

Measure what the user hears

Store an event time at each boundary. Use the same clock. Measure an acknowledgment and a useful answer as separate outputs.

  1. t0speech_started
  2. t1speech_stopped
  3. t2turn_committed
  4. t3model_started
  5. t4first_audio
  6. t5audio_played
  7. t6response_done
ENDPOINTING DELAY

t2 − t1

The system waits before it commits the user turn.
PERCEIVED RESPONSE LATENCY

t5 − t1

The user stops speaking and then hears the first agent audio.
MODEL + SYNTHESIS

t4 − t3

The agent starts work and produces its first audio.
FULL RESPONSE TIME

t6 − t1

The user stops speaking and the full response ends.

P50 shows the normal experience. P95 shows the slow experience that many users still encounter. Do not report only an average.

03 / SCORECARD

The metrics that matter

Use one main outcome metric. Add diagnostic metrics that explain why that outcome changed.

01 / OUTCOME

Did the agent complete the task?

A natural voice does not prove that the agent worked. Check the final application state and the result that the agent reported.

Task completion
Successful tasks ÷ attempted tasks
Final-state accuracy
The application contains the intended result
Tool accuracy
Correct tool, arguments, and execution order
Turns to completion
Conversation turns required for a successful task

YOUR FIRST SCORECARD

Track these six metrics first.

  1. 01Task completion rate
  2. 02Response latency, P50 and P95
  3. 03No-response rate
  4. 04Unwanted interruption rate
  5. 05Tool-call accuracy
  6. 06Cost per successful task

04 / EVALUATION

Test in three stages

Use a fixed scenario set. Run each scenario several times. Change one system factor at a time.

01 · CRAWL

Scripted input

Test prompts, tool calls, and final state with text or synthetic audio.

Fast · repeatable · limited realism

02 · WALK

Recorded audio

Test accents, noise, pauses, names, numbers, and corrections.

Real audio · fixed inputs

03 · RUN

Full conversation

Test multi-turn behavior, interruptions, recovery, and task completion.

Real interaction · more variation
KEEP FOR EACH FAILED RUN

Audio + transcript + event timeline + tool events + final application state

05 / FIRST BUILD

Build one thin path

Do not start with phone calls, many tools, or a large prompt. First, prove that one browser session can hear and answer.

  1. 01

    Open one voice session

    Connect the browser with WebRTC or a WebSocket. Show connect, mute, and stop controls.

  2. 02

    Complete one spoken turn

    Send microphone audio. Detect the turn end. Play the agent audio.

  3. 03

    Add one safe tool

    Use a read-only tool such as weather or a small local lookup.

  4. 04

    Add event timestamps

    Record the timeline events shown above. Calculate P50 and P95.

  5. 05

    Create ten test scenarios

    Include silence, noise, interruption, a name, a number, and one tool failure.

MINIMUM COMPONENTS

Browser
Microphone, speaker, and controls
Small server
API secret or short-lived client token
Voice API
Native speech, or STT + model + TTS
Event log
Times, transcript, tool result, and error
Test set
Ten fixed scenarios with expected results

The first useful output is a measured conversation. It is not a complete product.
